claims.claim: The GLB contains three named animation clips.
The model is a conventional skinned rig.
claims.evidence: No skins, JOINTS_0, WEIGHTS_0 or inverse-bind matrices; AXM rigged-gltf inspection refuses the skinned-rig claim

claims.claim: The model uses a reusable rigid-part hierarchy animation technique.
claims.evidence: Animation channels target named parent nodes whose children contain the visible body-part meshes

claims.claim: All three animations render and cross-fade correctly in AXM runtimes.
claims.evidence: No AXM live playback performed yet

claims.claim: The asset is cleared for public or commercial distribution.
claims.evidence: No applicable provider license receipt was supplied with the files

axmLearning.observedGap: AXM's current rigged GLB validator correctly understands deforming skinned rigs but treats rigid hierarchical character animation as a failed rig rather than a separate supported animation class.
axmLearning.reason: Rigid parts are cheap, readable and sufficient for stylized low-poly characters; skinned deformation remains necessary for bending organic meshes and retargeting.
